extension.description: A Kodi metadata scraper for TV shows, backed by your self-hosted Chronicle server. Unlike a normal scraper, it never talks to TheTVDB or any other upstream source directly -- it only ever asks Chronicle, which resolves-and-creates the item through whichever metadata providers you've already configured there, so Kodi always ends up seeing exactly what Chronicle itself would show for that title -- seasons and episodes, multi-source ratings, and all. Movies are a separate sibling addon, script.chronicle.scraper.movie -- install both if you track both. They have to be separate addons: Kodi resolves which script to run for a scrape by addon id alone, not by which extension point (movies vs tvshows) triggered the call, so one addon declaring both would silently run the wrong script for TV every time. Has its own "Connect to Chronicle" QR/PIN flow and its own API key, independent of the Movies addon -- open the addon (or its Settings) to connect. The corner status indicator lives in the Movies addon and covers both movies and TV shows together; this addon doesn't duplicate it. Neither addon writes a local NFO file of any kind -- Chronicle's own API is the source of truth both scrapers read from directly. It does have its own small background service that keeps Kodi's library in sync with newly-imported content, independent of the Movies addon -- see this version's changelog.
extension.news:
v1.13.8 - Same fix as the Movies addon's own v3.16.6 (this addon carries its own duplicate copy of movie_art_sync.py, used for cross-type NFO-rebuild resolution): the art-sync step now skips re-downloading poster/fanart when the exact same URL was already written last time and the local file's own size still matches, instead of unconditionally re-fetching from the remote CDN on every single scrape.
v1.13.7 - Fixes a very slow full-library scan (same root cause as the Movies addon's own v3.16.5, since this addon carries its own duplicate copies of movie_art_sync.py and tvshow_location.py -- see that release's notes for the full explanation). During an active scan, this addon's own show-location fallback (find_show_location -> _search_sources_for_show) re-lists every configured video source from scratch over the network for nearly every single show, even though that listing barely changes from one show to the next, seconds apart. Now caches each source's listing for 60 seconds.
v1.13.6 - New: this addon's own background service now reproduces what a manual "Scan Library" does once Kodi's native "Update library on startup" checkbox finishes its own too-early pass -- confirmed live that checkbox fires a real scan before network shares are mounted, so it sees an empty/unreachable source and finishes in under a minute instead of the real many-thousand-file scan a later manual call does. Per-user direction: fixed WITHOUT touching that checkbox -- it stays the only control, nothing new to configure. This addon's service now independently reads that same setting and, only if it's on, waits (bounded) for this addon's own source folder to actually be reachable, then fires one full scan itself, matching manual-scan semantics. Code-review fixes applied before release: doesn't fire a second overlapping scan while one's already running, doesn't fire twice on a device with both this and the Movies addon installed, and the reachability check itself can no longer hang forever on an unresponsive share.
v1.13.5 - Code-review fixes to Library Repair: repair_stale_shows() (the part of a repair that handles shows whose season folder moved on disk) fired an UNSCOPED VideoLibrary.Scan after removing the stale show -- confirmed this re-creates the exact same orphaned-episode problem Library Repair exists to fix (VideoLibrary.RemoveTVShow never truly deletes episode/file rows, so an unscoped rescan cascades into every other installed addon's own onScanFinished handler, not just this one) -- now scoped to only this addon's own source folder(s), same helper Preview/Repair already use elsewhere in the same file. Separately, the one truly destructive step of a real repair (finish_repair(execute=True)) had no exception handling at all, unlike every other step in the same flow -- a failure partway through used to surface as a raw, unhandled Kodi script error with no indication of what happened to the library; now shows the same friendly "see kodi.log" dialog as the rest of this feature.
v1.13.4 - Episodes now get their air date and runtime set on every scrape -- per-user report (2026-09-14): the air date was never read from Chronicle's own /tv/episode-details response at all (setPremiered() was simply never called for episodes, unlike the show/movie level). Runtime had a narrower version of the same gap: it only reached Kodi as a side effect of pushing a resume position, so an episode never played on this device got no runtime set either. Both are unconditional now, matching how movies/shows already work. Audited every other field the episode-details response carries against what Kodi's episode InfoTagVideo can actually represent -- title/plot/season/episode/year/cast/director/writer/ ratings/external ids/thumb art were already being set; there's nothing else left to add without a Kodi API method to receive it.
v1.13.3 - Repair Stuck Episodes (Preview and the real run) now shows a background progress indicator the instant you click, before detection/repair even starts -- per-user report (2026-09-14): with nothing shown until the (multi-second, on a real library) scan finished, a remote click looked exactly like it hadn't registered. The actual repair run keeps that indicator up and updating through its own backup and delete phases too, not just at the start. Also simplified every result/confirmation message down to the two numbers that matter -- total stuck episodes and how many shows they're spread across -- dropping the per-show example file path breakdown nobody asked to see.
v1.13.2 - REVERTED v1.13.1's datetime.strptime() priming fix: on the movie addon's identical copy of this module, it failed EVERY time at module-import time instead of fixing the rare original race, taking the ENTIRE background service down on every single Kodi startup. The original bug (one rare, tolerable failure during a huge concurrent burst) is far preferable to that. See lib/progress_sync.py's own note -- needs a real on-device repro before trying again.
v1.13.1 - Fixed a pre-existing, unrelated bug found live during a heavy rescan session (2026-09-13): lib/progress_sync.py's datetime.strptime() call could occasionally fail ("'NoneType' object is not callable") when Kodi's worker-thread pool raced its very first call in the process -- a well-known CPython lazy-import hazard, fixed by priming it once at module load. Also removed a few more pieces of now-dead code left over from the NFO removal below (unused chronicle_client._get_bytes(), unused legacy_nfo.py stash functions).
v1.13.0 - Removed local NFO writing entirely (write_nfo, tvshow.nfo via lib/tv_nfo_writer.py) -- per-user direction (2026-09-13) after it was suspected of interfering with TV show scanning reliability during a heavy rescan session. Chronicle's own API is the source of truth this scraper reads from directly; no local NFO was ever required for it to work. Paired with the same removal in the Movies addon (v3.16.0).
v1.12.3 - Repair Stuck Episodes now also fixes shows whose season folder Kodi can no longer find (renamed on disk) -- second step of the same repair, no new button. Resets watched status for those shows only; Chronicle resyncs it.
v1.12.2 - Adds a "What Is This?" button to Library Repair, shown as a real dialog (reported live 2026-09-13: the settings screen's own help text for these buttons wasn't visible at all on that device/skin, leaving zero explanation on screen of what a "stuck episode" even means). The full explanation no longer depends on that help panel ever rendering.
v1.12.1 - Fixes the entire Settings screen crashing on open (confirmed live 2026-09-13): lib/settings_mirror.py still referenced the write_streamdetails setting after v1.11.7 removed it from this addon's own settings.xml entirely, so opening Settings normally (not via a specific action button) raised "Invalid setting type" every time. Unrelated to the new v1.12.0 Library Repair feature itself -- a leftover from the per-episode NFO removal the day before -- but it blocked reaching Library Repair's own settings at all, since opening Settings is how every action in this addon (including the new one) gets reached in the first place.
v1.12.0 - New "Library Repair" settings action (three buttons: Preview, Repair Stuck Episodes, and Undo Last Repair). Root-caused live (2026-09-12): removing a TV show from Kodi's library -- even via a full "reset content type and rescan" -- never actually deletes that show's underlying episode/file database rows, only unlinks them. Those leftover ("orphaned") rows permanently block Kodi's own scanner from ever re-examining the exact same files again, no matter how many times the show is removed and rescanned -- confirmed live on a real device, one show permanently capped at 2 of 30 real episodes, another at 52 of 91, for months, regardless of any number of rescans. This is the fix: a settings action that finds and removes exactly those orphaned entries on THIS device's own Kodi library, with a mandatory verified backup made first, a clear before-you-commit summary of what it found, and an Undo action that reverses precisely the most recent repair from its own backup if anything looks wrong afterward. See lib/library_repair.py's own module docstring for the full safety design.
v1.11.7 - Per-user direction (2026-09-12): this addon no longer writes a per-episode NFO file, ever. Root cause: Kodi's NfoUrl action for an episode carries no show context whatsoever (not even a folder path), and unlike a failed show-level NfoUrl call (harmless -- Kodi falls back to its own normal find/getepisodelist flow), a failed episode-level one aborts the REST of that show's scan entirely with no fallback of its own. That's a structural Kodi limitation, not something either side of this pipeline can route around -- so the fix is to never let Chronicle's own generated content trigger that fragile path in the first place. Nothing is lost: the ordinary find/getepisodelist/getepisodedetails scan already delivers every field an episode NFO would have, and the Movies addon's watch_rating_sync.py already keeps rating/resume/watched status current on anything already in a device's library directly via VideoLibrary.Set*Details, independent of any local file. Confirmed live: a real household show that used to stall partway through a rescan (missing/incomplete NFOs on specific episodes aborting the rest of the scan) now completes in one pass. Chronicle's own NFO-rebuild queue will also stop offering this addon episode work at all (server-side change, no addon action needed) -- see the Chronicle server's own changelog for that half of the fix.
v1.11.6 - Root-caused live (2026-09-12): during an active library scan, Chronicle's own scheduled NFO-generation sweep and this addon's live per-item pushes were independently rebuilding and writing the same freshly-scanned item's NFO within seconds of each other -- pure waste that competed with the scan itself for the same server/IO capacity, slowing the whole scan down. service.py now sends Chronicle a short heartbeat while Kodi's own scan OR this addon's own scraper-activity tail is still running, so the server-side sweep pauses itself for the duration instead of contending with it. No settings change needed -- this is on for everyone automatically.
v1.11.5 - Fixes the actual cause of a real household show stuck at exactly 5 of 38 episodes no matter how many times it was rescanned, restarted, or removed-and-rescanned: v1.11.4 above said episode-level NfoUrl calls could safely stay unhandled because "Kodi's existing fallback already handles those correctly once the show itself is identified" -- confirmed live this was WRONG. A failed show-level NfoUrl call does fall back cleanly, but a failed EPISODE-level one does not: kodi.log showed Kodi abandoning the rest of that show's episode scan entirely the moment the very first episode's NfoUrl call came back empty, never falling back to a normal getepisodelist/getepisodedetails pass for that show at all. Once Chronicle's own write_nfo feature had written a sidecar .nfo next to every episode file, that first failure landed on episode 1 every time, silently capping the show at whatever had scanned in before its NFOs existed. Now resolves the episode directly via a new Chronicle endpoint (tv/resolve-episode-by-external-id) using whatever provider id the episode's own NFO carries (tmdb/imdb/tvdb) -- there is still no show-context fallback available for an episode the way there is for a show, but a real id on the NFO (the common case for anything write_nfo itself wrote) now resolves correctly instead of failing.
v1.11.4 - Implements the "NfoUrl" scraper action for shows (a documented gap until now): Kodi calls this when a show's own tvshow.nfo already exists on disk (e.g. from a prior tool like tinyMediaManager) instead of calling find(), and this addon always just failed it silently. Confirmed live that Kodi tolerates the failure and falls back to a normal title+year search anyway, so this was never a hard "zero episodes" blocker on its own -- but every one of those already-organized shows paid for a wasted, always-failing round trip first, and lost the chance to be identified precisely from whatever provider ids the existing NFO already carries. Fixes both: now resolves directly via the NFO's own imdb/tmdb/tvdb id when present, falling back to title+year only if none of those resolve. Episode-level NfoUrl calls are deliberately still left alone (an episode's own NFO carries no show context at all to resolve from) -- Kodi's existing fallback already handles those correctly once the show itself is identified.
v1.11.3 - Root-caused a real household library never fully scanning in: get_episode_details() called find_show_location() unconditionally, on EVERY episode -- re-resolving the exact same (folder, tvshowid) pair for every single episode of a show via a JSON-RPC round-trip back into Kodi's own API (with its own retry-and-sleep on a miss). During a first-time scan of 100+ shows, with Kodi running many of these scraper callbacks concurrently, this became self-inflicted contention on Kodi's own API from Kodi's own scan -- shows sat with only their most-recently- processed handful of episodes ever committed, no exception anywhere (in this addon's log or Kodi's own) to point at the cause, since a scraper callback that doesn't return in time just looks like one Kodi never got around to. Caches a show's resolved location for 15 minutes so every episode after the first one skips the redundant lookup entirely.
v1.11.2 - getartwork (the picker behind "Choose Art", and part of a full Refresh) never worked: Kodi passes back this show's default uniqueid (imdb, since Chronicle's own NFOs always mark it default="true") as a bare string like "tt27497393" for this one action, instead of this addon's own opaque lookup string that find/getdetails exchange -- _resolve_lookup_id had no case for that shape, silently returned nothing every time, and Kodi's "Choose Art" showed zero options for every show, for every user, with nothing distinctive in the log to point at (just a generic "can't parse lookup string" warning that looked like noise from an unrelated addon). Adds a new Chronicle server lookup (GET tv/resolve-by-external-id) and wires it in as a third case in _resolve_lookup_id. Confirmed live: getartwork now correctly resolves a show's imdb id instead of failing to parse it.
v1.11.1 - Two corrections to v1.11.0's new-content scan-signal feature, both found during review before it ever shipped in a release build:
(1) The triggered scan now only ever touches the source folder(s) THIS addon is actually configured as the scraper for on this device (read live from Kodi's own video database -- never cached, and never inferred from Chronicle's own server-side folder paths, since a device's local source naming has no reliable relationship to those). Previously it called VideoLibrary.Scan with no directory at all, which scans every configured source regardless of content type -- on a device with movie folders too, that meant a TV-triggered scan was also touching movie folders this addon has no relationship with at all.
(2) The periodic check is now OFF by default (was: always checked every 3 minutes). Reason: a triggered VideoLibrary.Scan fires Kodi's global onScanFinished event, which every other addon's own Monitor reacts to independently -- confirmed live that this cascades into Chronicle_Scrobbler's own VideoLibrary.Clean and SIMKL Scrobbler's own full sync pass, not just this addon's work. This device still always checks once when Kodi starts (catches anything imported overnight with zero configuration), and a new "Periodically check for new content" setting lets you opt back into recurring checks at an interval you choose (default 120 minutes, was effectively 3).
v1.11.0 - New: this addon now has its own background service, independent of the Movies addon. It polls Chronicle every few minutes for "new movie/TV content was imported" and, if due, triggers its own local library scan (VideoLibrary.Scan) to pick it up -- closes a real gap where a brand-new episode file never got discovered at all until someone noticed and clicked "Update Library" by hand, since VideoLibrary.Refresh* only works on an item Kodi already has a library entry for. Pull, not push: this device polls and scans itself via its own local xbmc.executeJSONRPC, so nothing here needs "Allow remote control via HTTP" turned on. Previously this addon relied on the Movies addon's own background service for anything running in the background at all -- as of this release it needs nothing else installed for this feature; "no duplicated service" is limited to NFO-rebuild-on-scan and the corner status indicator, which still require the Movies addon.
v1.10.2 - Per-user report (2026-09-09): an episode marked watched still showed a progress percentage in Kodi. Same root cause and fix as the Movies addon's v3.14.1: a device's own stale local resume point (partial playback never finished on that device) was left completely untouched even as the same reconciliation pass set playcount=1 for the watched status. Now explicitly zeroed whenever an episode is marked watched.
v1.10.1 - Fixed a gap in v1.10.0 below: a settings.xml default="..." only ever applies to a value Kodi has never persisted, so simply changing write_nfo's shipped default did nothing for an already-installed copy of this addon. Added a one-time code migration (lib/settings_upgrade.py) that actually turns it on for an existing install the moment any part of this addon next runs -- no Kodi restart, and no manual settings change needed.
v1.10.0 - "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" now defaults ON (was OFF) -- this addon's own copy of that setting must agree with the movie addon's for a rebuild pass to actually write anything for TV shows/episodes, and leaving it off by default meant episode/ rating/progress changes could silently never reach Kodi for a library that already had local NFOs. HTTP calls to Chronicle (show/episode details, search) now retry twice with a short backoff on a transient network failure -- root-caused a real "show has zero poster options at all" report to exactly this: a single timeout during a full-library rescan's request burst, with no local-art fallback the way movies have, permanently skipped artwork for that show. Chronicle's own tv/details endpoint now also logs a warning when an item has no poster candidates at all, for parity with the movie side.
v1.9.0 - Per-user request: speed up getting a Chronicle metadata change out to Kodi. Editing a show or episode in Chronicle now writes its NFO straight to disk immediately (server-side) and pushes a targeted refresh to this device if it's already reported its own internal id for that item -- instead of waiting for a manual/scheduled "Recreate local NFO" pass or this device's own next library scan. Device registration itself (the piece that lets Chronicle reach this instance at all) lives in the Movies addon, same as "Recreate local NFO" and the corner status indicator -- this addon just reports its own tvshowid/episodeid back during a rebuild pass, same gate as its NFO writes already use.
v1.8.0 - "Recreate local NFO" now fetches each show/episode NFO's own document pre-built from Chronicle's server (a new companion plugin, Chronicle.Plugin.Kodi.NFO) instead of building the XML on this device in Python -- same document, same fields, just assembled on the more capable machine. This addon now only splices in the two things Chronicle's server structurally cannot know: Kodi's own streamdetails probe (episodes only) and local art files already sitting on disk. No behaviour change for ordinary library scans (NFO writing was, and remains, rebuild-pass-only) -- this only affects how the "Recreate local NFO" action itself builds each document.
v1.7.0 - Per-user request (2026-09-05): an episode completed on one Shield stayed permanently unwatched on another, with no error -- Chronicle clears its own resume-percent/ timestamp the moment an item is marked watched (nothing left to "resume"), so the existing resume reconciliation had no signal at all to work with for a fully-finished episode. Watched status is now reconciled the same way resume position already was, using its own signal (Chronicle's watched flag and completion time, which are never cleared) -- whichever side is more recent pushes its playcount/lastplayed to the other. Sibling of the movie addon's identical v3.8.0 fix.
v1.6.0 - Per-user redirect (2026-08-30): "I don't want a separate sync task in Kodi for ratings. this needs to happen with the scraper automatically as part of the scrape process." Same change as the Movies addon's v3.6.0 (see its own changelog for the full explanation) -- rating and resume reconciliation now happen inline inside getdetails/getepisodedetails, replacing Chronicle_Scrobbler's retired periodic sync. Applies to shows (rating only -- Kodi has no per-show resume concept) and episodes (rating + resume, same "most recent wins" rule via Kodi's lastplayed). Resolving the show's own tvshowid (needed for the episode-level resume lookup) now happens on every scrape rather than only during a rebuild pass -- one extra small VideoLibrary lookup per episode scrape, the TV-side equivalent of what the Movies addon already did unconditionally. v1.5.5 - Writes each actor's Chronicle-resolved headshot into the NFO's <actor><thumb> tag when Chronicle has one (Phase 6 of the People feature, docs/plans/2026-08-28-people-section-design.md) -- Kodi's own actor NFO schema already supports this, it just never had anything to put there before. No visible change until enough people have been resolved with real photos server-side. v1.5.4 - Per-user correction (2026-08-29): "I only ever want them to open the regular settings window, not whatever [the old action-list menu] is" -- launching this addon from Kodi's Add-on browser now goes straight to Settings instead of showing a Dialog().select() menu first. Test Connection, previously only reachable from that menu, now has its own action button in Settings' Connection category (Edit Connection/Change Chronicle URL already had theirs). v1.5.3 - Fixes invalid XML in resources/settings.xml (a "--" inside an actual XML comment, not just element text) caught by a repo-wide sweep after this same mistake showed up several times tonight in other files. No functional/behavior change; a full sweep of every .xml/.csproj/.props/.targets file under this whole project tree confirms nothing else is affected. v1.5.2 - Per-user request (2026-08-29): "each of the add-ons could check each other for the chronicle URL and just copy it in from another working add-on... save the typing." "Edit Connection"'s URL prompt now checks the other installed Chronicle addons (Scraper Movies, Scrobbler) for an already-configured chronicle_url and pre-fills the entry dialog with the first one found, instead of always starting blank -- still one explicit confirm step, never silently auto-connects. A sibling that isn't installed, or has nothing set yet itself, is simply skipped. v1.5.1 - Packaging fix (2026-08-29): opening this addon threw an immediate "Error - check log" with no dialog and no request ever reaching Chronicle -- confirmed live on a second device (upstairs Shield). Root cause: default.py imports lib.device_auth.DeviceAuthManager, but that module is deliberately NOT checked into this addon's own lib/ (build.ps1's SharedFiles mechanism is supposed to copy it in from the sibling Movie addon's lib/ at build time, so there's exactly one source of truth instead of two copies that could drift). The zip shipped for v1.5.0 was built by hand (Compress-Archive) instead of through build.ps1, so that copy step never ran and the module was simply missing -- a ModuleNotFoundError the instant the script loaded, before show_menu() or anything else in it had a chance to run. No source change here; this version exists purely to force a build.ps1 rebuild with the shared file correctly included. v1.5.0 - New: the main menu now shows connection status (and WHO's connected -- "Connected as {name}", via GET /users/me) directly in the menu heading, before you'd ever click "Edit Connection" -- per-user request (2026-08-28): "update the scrapers and the scrobbler to show that they're connected or not before they try to make a connection... say who was connected also." 5s-bounded so an unreachable server doesn't make the menu itself feel stuck; falls back to the last-known name (cached in a new hidden connected_display_name setting) rather than regressing to a bare "Connected" on a transient network blip. v1.4.0 - Episode NFOs still never got written during a rebuild even after v1.3.0's write_nfo-mirroring fix landed: confirmed live via kodi.log (2026-08-28) that lib/tvshow_location.py get_episode() -- which asks VideoLibrary.GetEpisodes(tvshowid) for an episode's own file path -- came back empty for essentially every episode processed during a rebuild, not because the file was missing (the movie addon's nfo_rebuild.py had already found a real path for every one of them, before any refresh was issued) but because VideoLibrary.RefreshEpisode()'s own in-flight scrape tears down that exact episode's library row until the scrape's own getepisodedetails() callback returns -- the episode was asking VideoLibrary about itself, from inside itself, before it was done. New lib/episode_path_cache.py (same file as the movie addon's copy, duplicated for the same reason legacy_nfo.py/rebuild_state.py are) stashes each episode's already-known-good file path right before nfo_rebuild.py issues its refresh; get_episode_details() now falls back to that stash whenever the live VideoLibrary lookup comes back empty. If both come up empty (shouldn't happen in practice now), that episode's NFO write is skipped with a clear kodi.log warning instead of the previous silent no-op. v1.3.0 - New: changing "Recreate local NFO file from Chronicle's data" or "Include technical file info" (via Settings) now offers to apply the identical change to the sibling script.chronicle.scraper.movie addon too, if installed. Root cause of a live 2026-08-28 report ("NFO rebuild stuck at the same count for over an hour"): the two addons keep entirely separate settings.xml files, and this addon's write_nfo had silently drifted to off while the movie side's stayed on -- an in-progress rebuild kept successfully re-scraping every TV episode with nothing ever actually writing to disk, and nothing in kodi.log said why. New lib/settings_mirror.py (same file as the movie addon's copy, duplicated for the same reason nfo_rebuild.py's other helpers are); asks once per change, covering both settings together, and only when the sibling addon is actually installed. v1.2.3 - Code-review fixes to the Connect flow: a QR pairing that was approved on the phone but whose one-time key never reached this device (e.g. a poll that timed out client-side even though the request actually completed) used to leave the QR window stuck open forever -- it now shows a clear error and asks you to try Connect again. The Settings status field could briefly flash back to "Not connected" immediately after a successful connect -- fixed. Declining the loopback-URL warning now actually cancels the connect instead of proceeding against that URL anyway. New "Change Chronicle URL" action (main menu and Settings) is the first way to correct a wrong URL once one is saved -- there was previously no way to do this short of editing settings.xml by hand. A malformed response from Chronicle during device-auth now shows a specific error instead of crashing to a generic "Connect failed unexpectedly". lib/device_auth.py is now synced from the movie addon's copy at build time instead of being hand-maintained as a second, driftable copy. v1.2.2 - v1.2.1 fixed _initiate()'s own cross-instance chronicle_url read but missed an identical one in _poll_loop() -- confirmed live: after approving the device on the phone, the QR window never closed, with "Poll error: unknown url type: '/api/v1/auth/device/{code}/poll'" in the log -- a schemeless, hostless URL, meaning _poll_loop()'s own independent ADDON.getSetting('chronicle_url') read came back empty even though _initiate()'s POST (already fixed to use self._base_url) had worked moments earlier and produced a real QR code. _poll_loop() now also uses self._base_url. v1.2.1 - Root cause of v1.2.0's URL-entry-still-not-working reports found via logging: confirmed live that default.py's own ADDON.setSetting('chronicle_url', ...) is not reliably visible to device_auth.py's SEPARATE xbmcaddon.Addon() instance's very next getSetting('chronicle_url') call -- same process, same addon, same settings.xml, one line apart, and still empty. Kodi's Addon() binding apparently doesn't guarantee cross-instance read-your-own-write consistency. DeviceAuthManager now takes the resolved URL as a constructor parameter instead of re-reading it independently -- default.py hands over the value it just resolved (or prompted for and saved) directly, sidestepping the cross-instance question entirely rather than continuing to chase it through Kodi's settings storage. v1.2.0 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, per user request: the Chronicle URL now has exactly ONE entry point instead of two. Settings' own chronicle_url field is now read-only (enable="false") -- it was never reliably editable there to begin with (v1.1.5/v1.1.7's own investigation confirmed Kodi's on-screen-keyboard edit to that field doesn't always land in the saved value, even after the whole Settings dialog closes). "Connect to Chronicle" is renamed "Edit Connection" and is now the only place a URL is ever entered: it prompts via a proven-reliable dialog ONLY when there isn't already a saved URL, so an already-connected reconnect skips straight to the QR window with no prompt -- a working URL is never typed twice. Also removed: the auto-bounce to Settings on first run (no longer needed, since "Edit Connection" is directly reachable from the main menu and handles an empty URL itself), and all of v1.1.5-1.1.7's Action(Back)/reopen-Settings/settle-wait/fallback-prompt machinery in default.py and device_auth.py -- none of it is necessary anymore now that Settings' text field is out of the picture entirely. v1.1.7 - Two fixes from a confirmed live report: closing Settings (v1.1.5) did NOT fix it after all -- chronicle_url still read empty even after the dialog was fully closed, not just delayed, meaning the on-screen-keyboard edit to that field isn't reliably landing in the underlying setting at all on some setups. _initiate() now falls back to a single guaranteed-reliable xbmcgui.Dialog().input() prompt when chronicle_url is still empty after everything else has been tried, saves it explicitly, and proceeds -- only appears when the Settings-based path has actually failed, never adding friction to a working connect. Also: the "Status" field in Settings was showing "Connected" purely because an api_key from a past successful connection was still saved, even while chronicle_url was empty and every current Connect attempt was failing outright -- _refresh_auth_status() now requires both, matching _is_configured()'s own check. v1.1.6 - Settings now reopens automatically right after v1.1.5's Action(Back) close (Addon.OpenSettings, non-blocking, unlike ADDON.openSettings()), so the forced close reads as a quick visual blip instead of dumping you back at whatever was behind Settings for the rest of the Connect flow -- Kodi's own window manager should restore focus to wherever you left off (e.g. "Connect to Chronicle" itself) automatically. The QR window then appears on top of that reopened Settings screen. v1.1.5 - Root cause finally confirmed by reading settings.xml directly moments after a failed Connect attempt: chronicle_url was still at its empty default over a minute after the user typed a URL and could see it sitting in the field -- not a timing race (v1.1.4's settle-wait didn't help, because there was nothing to wait FOR), an ORDERING one. Kodi's addon Settings dialog only writes settings.xml to disk when the whole dialog closes, not per-field as focus moves between controls, and "Connect to Chronicle" is a button INSIDE that same still-open dialog. _connect_to_chronicle() now closes Settings first (Action(Back), only when Window.IsActive(addonsettings) confirms it's actually open -- a no-op from the main-menu path, never risking closing the wrong window) before reading chronicle_url and connecting. v1.1.4 - Fixes the actual bug behind v1.1.1's (reverted) URL-confirm prompt, without bringing back the prompt. Confirmed live with v1.1.2/v1.1.3's own logging: chronicle_url read back completely empty immediately after typing a URL and clicking "Connect to Chronicle" from inside the still-open Settings dialog, for a URL that WAS saved correctly moments later -- Kodi's Settings dialog does not always flush a just-edited field to settings.xml synchronously with an action button fired from that same dialog. _initiate() now waits 500ms (imperceptible alongside the real network round-trip that follows) before its first read of chronicle_url, giving Kodi's flush time to land -- fixes both a first-time URL entry and switching to a different URL, with no added dialog or retyping. v1.1.3 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: reverts v1.1.1's "confirm the URL before connecting" prompt. The new v1.1.2 logging caught it live: the prompt added a mandatory on-screen-keyboard URL retype to every single Connect attempt, and the actual bug report that led to this revert was the user backing out of that unexpected prompt within ~2 seconds -- not a stale URL ever being used. "Connect to Chronicle" now goes straight to the QR window again, same as before v1.1.1. If a URL edited in Settings and immediately connected-to via the in-Settings action button still ever reads stale, close Settings fully first and click Connect from the main menu instead -- that path always reads the already-flushed value. Diagnostic logging (step-by-step trace, distinct per-addon log prefix) from v1.1.2 stays in place. v1.1.2 - Diagnostic logging only, no behavior change: the Connect flow (default.py's _connect_to_chronicle) now logs every step -- the URL read from disk, what the URL prompt returned, whether it changed, and DeviceAuthManager.run()'s own progress through _initiate()/QR-download/QRDialog construction/doModal(), plus a caught-and-logged traceback if anything in that call raises (a RunScript-launched script has no visible crash surface otherwise -- an unhandled exception would look identical to "the connection window just never showed up"). Also: log prefix changed from the shared "[ChronicleScraper]" to "[ChronicleScraperTV]" -- it was identical to the sibling Movies addon's own prefix, making it impossible to tell which addon a given kodi.log line came from when both are installed. Added while investigating a live report: switched the URL, clicked Connect, and got the new URL-confirm prompt but not the QR window afterward. v1.1.1 - "Connect to Chronicle" now confirms the Chronicle URL directly (a text prompt, pre-filled with whatever's currently saved) instead of trusting chronicle_url on disk. Confirmed live: switching URLs in Settings and immediately clicking "Connect to Chronicle" (the action button lives inside that same still-open Settings dialog) built the QR code against the OLD URL -- a just-typed text field's value isn't guaranteed to be flushed to settings.xml before Kodi launches the RunScript action as a brand new process, so the fresh process could read stale data even though the new value was visibly still sitting in the field. This also fixes the fresh-install case: opening the addon for the first time now prompts for the URL right in the Connect flow instead of requiring a value to already be saved before Connect can do anything with it. v1.1.0 - This addon now shows up as a launchable entry in the Kodi add-on browser and has its own "Connect to Chronicle" QR/PIN flow -- previously it only ever exposed the xbmc.metadata.scraper.tvshows hook, with no script entry point at all, so connecting it meant manually copying the URL and API key over from Chronicle Scraper (Movies)'s settings. New default.py (own menu: Test Connection / Connect to Chronicle / Open Settings -- deliberately not duplicating Movies' NFO-rebuild menu entry, see that file's own docstring), lib/device_auth.py and lib/qr_dialog.py ported from the Movies addon, resources/qr_panel.png copied over. api_key is now a hidden setting set by the QR flow rather than a plain text field you paste into by hand, matching the Movies addon's UX. Also: device_auth.py's "Could not contact the Chronicle server" dialog now shows the actual reason (empty URL, DNS failure, connection refused, timeout, HTTP error, etc.) instead of the same generic text for every failure. v1.0.1 - Three fixes, all found in code review: (1) lib/legacy_nfo.py's stash directory was still under special://profile/addon_data/{addon_id}/ in this addon's copy, scoped to this addon's own id -- meaning a TV show's stashed legacy-NFO data (harvested by this addon's delete step) could never be found by the re-scrape that consumes it, since that re-scrape also runs from this same addon's process but the path itself was never actually reachable in the intended cross-addon case. Now stashes under special://temp/chronicle_scraper/, matching rebuild_state.py and activity_tracker.py. (2) settings.xml had an invalid XML comment (a literal "--" inside the comment body, which XML never allows outside the opening/closing delimiters) -- replaced with an em dash. (3) strings.po's #32092 help text had unescaped literal quote marks inside its msgid, breaking that string's parsing -- now escaped to match the convention used everywhere else in this file. v1.0.0 - Split out of script.chronicle.scraper (now script.chronicle.scraper.movie) as its own addon, so Kodi can actually invoke the TV scraper -- see that addon's v3.0.0 changelog entry for the full root-cause explanation. Same code as tvshow_scraper.py always had (the v2.13.2 endOfDirectory fix and the v2.13.3 rebuild-pass-only NFO gating), just finally reachable.
